independent.summary: `source` is the one record field still built from caller text and it is not capped, so the new module header's and docs' claim that "a refusal line is these plus a few hundred characters of this module's own, however large the request was" is false: `routes/mcp.js:759` interpolates `req.body.method` verbatim into `source` on the session_missing path (the same value `rpc` now clips to 64), and the bridge's `toolFailure` detail interpolates free-string tool arguments (`routes/bridge.js:271,274,443,526`, all `z.string()` with no max). A ~100 kB `method` or `reply_to` therefore still writes a ~100 kB record line — gated behind a valid bearer on a deployed /mcp (and behind BRIDGE_TOKEN on the bridge), so the unauthenticated hole the item targeted is genuinely closed, but in the dev/open gate configuration (`MCP_TOKEN` unset, non-prod) the session_missing path is reachable unauthenticated and the record is unbounded again. Also latent: `...extra` spreads after `rpc`/`tool`/`requestId` in `mcpLogRecord`, so a future call site passing one of those keys in `extra` silently bypasses its cap (today only literals and counts are passed, so no live bug).

The `auth` presentation field and the verbose-only token logging are untouched; no credential handling changes.
No billing, pricing, usage-metering or model-cost code is involved.
No deletes, migrations or overwrites — the change only truncates strings when building a log line.
No outbound calls, and the JSON-RPC response body is deliberately left byte-identical (the id is still echoed verbatim).
Only a lib file, two test files, a new test file and a docs paragraph; no deploy, env or version config.
